ut.description: Ultrasonic thickness testing and UT weld inspection for Huntsville aerospace, defense, test-stand, pressure and plant equipment, at your site. Get a UT quote.
ut.h1: Ultrasonic Testing (UT) Inspection in Huntsville, Alabama
ut.html:
Atlantis NDT carries out ultrasonic thickness testing and ultrasonic weld examination for industrial and engineering sites in the Huntsville area: pressure vessels and gas piping, test-stand and ground-support equipment, welded steel structures, plate and forgings, and plant utilities. Technicians travel to your site with calibrated instruments, follow a written procedure, and report against the specification your customer or engineer names. Send your ultrasonic scope for a quote and expect a reply within one business day.

Where ultrasonic testing is used in Huntsville

Few American cities have an industrial profile as concentrated as Huntsville's. Redstone Arsenal hosts the Army's aviation and missile commands and its space and missile defense command. NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center, established in 1960, developed the Saturn V and works on the Space Launch System. Cummings Research Park, started in 1962 beside the arsenal, now holds roughly three hundred companies, many in aerospace and defense. Around that core sit engine plants, automotive suppliers and a wider manufacturing base of a couple of hundred firms.

Ultrasonic work in that environment is mostly about proving that welded and pressure-containing hardware is sound and has not thinned. High-pressure gas bottles and manifolds, cryogenic and propellant piping, vessel shells and heads, test-stand structures and heavy lifting fixtures all carry loads that make wall thickness and weld integrity matter. Machine shops and structural fabricators supporting these programs also need thickness checks on plate and forgings before machining, and on tooling that has been in service for years. Utility piping at the plants and research facilities, from steam to compressed air, rounds out the routine survey work.

What UT finds and what it misses on aerospace and defense hardware

Ultrasonic testing measures how long sound takes to cross a part and return, which converts to thickness, and it displays reflections from internal discontinuities. For a welded steel structure or a pressure boundary this makes it a direct way to find lack of fusion, cracks, slag and laminations that cannot be seen from outside. On plate and forged stock it finds laminations and internal discontinuities before expensive machining begins.

Limits matter in a place where margins are tight. Thin sheet and small-diameter tubing are often too thin for conventional contact probes to resolve, and the near-surface dead zone can hide flaws close to the entry surface. Complex geometry, tight radii and fillets reduce the scan area, and coarse or anisotropic grain in some castings and welds scatters sound. Surface-breaking cracks that are tight and shallow are better found by penetrant or magnetic particle methods. We state what ultrasonic testing can and cannot resolve on your specific component during scope review, because a clean scan on a part that was never scannable proves nothing.

Codes and specifications that govern the work

Technique follows ASME Section V: Article 4 for weld examination, Article 5 for ultrasonic examination of materials such as plate and forgings, and Article 23 (SE-797) for contact thickness measurement. ASTM E164 covers contact examination of weldments, E114 straight-beam contact examination, and E797 thickness measurement. Acceptance depends on the item. Pressure vessels built to ASME Section VIII Division 1 refer to Mandatory Appendix 12, process and gas piping to ASME B31.3 (paragraph 344.6 and Table 341.3.2), and structural steel to AWS D1.1. In-service vessels and piping follow API 510 and API 570, with the owner's authorized inspector holding responsibility and Atlantis supplying the measurements.

Aerospace and defense customers often add their own specifications and flow-down clauses. Tell us which documents your purchase order or contract references and we write the procedure to them, subject to review by an ASNT Level III. In Alabama, boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act administered by the Alabama Department of Workforce, and OSHA's process safety rule at 29 CFR 1910.119(j) applies at covered plants.

Thickness surveys on pressure and gas systems

A thickness survey begins with a drawing. Measurement points are marked at locations that matter for the damage mechanism: elbows and tees on piping, the bottom of a horizontal vessel, and the area below a nozzle. The surface is cleaned, a dual-element probe is calibrated on a step block of the same alloy, and the technician records the nominal and minimum wall if given. The A-scan display is watched on every reading, since it shows when a gauge has locked onto a lamination or a doubled echo.

Alloy matters. Sound travels at a different speed in carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminum, so calibration on a block of the same material is not optional, and probes are selected for the grain structure. Hot surfaces call for high-temperature probes and couplant with a temperature correction. Readings are logged by point, which makes later surveys comparable and lets an engineer calculate a corrosion rate and remaining life for the owner.

Weld examination with angle beams

Angle-beam examination uses a probe on a wedge that directs a shear wave into the weld at an angle, commonly 45, 60 or 70 degrees. A distance-amplitude curve is built on a reference block with side-drilled holes, the technician scans along and across the weld from available sides, and each indication is evaluated for amplitude, length and position. Weld geometry, root condition and plate thickness shape the plan. Thicker structural welds on test stands and fixtures suit shear-wave work well, while thin-wall joints are sometimes better handled by another method.

Plate and forging examination uses straight-beam probes in a scan pattern defined by the specification, looking for laminations and internal discontinuities and sometimes recording back-wall loss as a sign of coupling or attenuation problems. The report ties each finding to a position on a sketch so the supplier or engineer can disposition it.

Who does the work

Level II technicians perform and interpret the examination under Atlantis's written practice, which is based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Procedures are written to the code or specification and approved by an ASNT Level III, who also reviews reports. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. Atlantis has no office in Huntsville; technicians are mobilized to your site for the agreed scope. Many programs here require personnel records, procedure approvals and calibration traceability before anyone touches hardware, so supply the requirement early and the proposal will list exactly which records come with the crew.

What the UT report contains

The report names the component, drawing and serial or tag, the procedure and revision, the governing specification and acceptance criteria, and the instrument, probes, wedges and reference blocks with their calibration status. It identifies the technician and certification level. Thickness work shows the nominal wall, minimum if supplied, and every reading by location. Weld and material work lists each reportable indication with location, depth, length and amplitude, and gives an accept or reject call with a sketch. Calibration sheets and raw readings are kept so the customer's quality group or an auditor can reconstruct the result.

Planning a UT job in Huntsville

Access to Redstone Arsenal and to many research park facilities involves gate access, visitor or contractor badging, citizenship and background checks for some programs, and escort rules. Sort this out with your site contact before the crew travels, because it can set the schedule more than any technical issue. Summers in the Tennessee Valley are hot and humid, which affects surface temperature and couplant behavior outdoors, and winters are mild with occasional hard freezes that can matter on exposed steel. Large structures, such as test stands, usually need scaffold or lift access that the owner provides. Controlled areas may restrict cameras and electronics, so we ask about instrument approvals when we scope the job.

UT, MT or PT for Huntsville hardware

Use ultrasonic testing for thickness and internal flaws. For surface cracks in steel components such as fixtures, lifting lugs and fasteners, magnetic particle inspection in Huntsville is faster and more sensitive. For aluminum, stainless, nickel and titanium parts that cannot be magnetized, liquid penetrant testing in Huntsville is the surface method. Many hardware jobs use two methods on the same weld. The general ultrasonic testing overview explains the method nationally, the Huntsville inspection services hub collects the work we support locally, and the ultimate guide to ultrasonic testing covers fundamentals.

Training your own UT staff

Companies in the research park and supplier base often qualify their own technicians. Atlantis provides UT Level 1 training and UT Level 2 training built on SNT-TC-1A, with practice in the ultrasonic testing simulator. The employer certifies under its written practice, and the Huntsville NDT training page explains how courses are delivered. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows the hours a candidate needs.

faq.q: Can ultrasonic testing be used on aerospace and defense hardware in Huntsville?
faq.a: Yes, on thickness checks, welds in steel and pressure parts, plate and forgings. We write the procedure to the specification your customer provides, and we say up front where geometry or thickness puts a part beyond conventional UT.

faq.q: What UT work do test stands and ground support equipment need?
faq.a: Typical work includes weld examination on structural members and fixtures, thickness surveys on gas and propellant piping and vessels, and checks on lifting hardware before reuse.

faq.q: Does the material change how ultrasonic thickness readings are taken?
faq.a: Yes. Sound speed differs in carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminum, so the instrument is calibrated on a step block of the same alloy before and during the survey.

faq.q: Can ultrasonic testing find surface cracks on small parts?
faq.a: Not reliably. Tight surface cracks on small or thin components are better found with magnetic particle or liquid penetrant methods, which we can pair with UT on the same job.

faq.q: What records come with the crew for a controlled program?
faq.a: We provide procedures with Level III approval, personnel qualification records under the written practice, and calibration records for instruments and blocks. Send your requirements at the quote stage.

faq.q: Do you have an office in Huntsville?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Huntsville. Technicians are mobilized to your facility for the agreed scope, with equipment calibrated before travel.

faq.q: Who evaluates the ultrasonic indications?
faq.a: A Level II technician evaluates indications against the stated criteria, an ASNT Level III reviews procedure and report, and your engineer or authorized inspector makes any fitness-for-service decision.

faq.q: How are access and badging handled on a controlled site?
faq.a: You provide the site contact and badge requirements, and we submit personnel details in advance. Access rules can set the schedule, so raise them before the visit is planned.

faq.q: Can my own technicians train for ultrasonic testing?
faq.a: Yes. Level 1 and Level 2 UT courses prepare technicians for thickness gauging and weld evaluation, and your company completes the practical and certification under its written practice.

mt.title: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MPI) | Huntsville, AL MT
mt.description: On-site magnetic particle inspection (MT) for Huntsville aerospace fixtures, defense hardware, lifting gear, steel welds and castings, run at your site. Get a quote.
mt.h1: Magnetic Particle Inspection (MT) in Huntsville, Alabama
mt.html:
Atlantis NDT provides magnetic particle inspection on ferromagnetic steel hardware around Huntsville: fixtures and tooling, lifting and handling equipment, welded structures, fasteners, shafts and forgings, and weld repairs. Technicians travel to your site with yokes, particles and ultraviolet lighting, work to a written procedure, and report against the specification your customer or engineer names. Request a magnetic particle quote with your component list and you will hear back within one business day.

Where magnetic particle inspection is used in Huntsville

Huntsville's economy runs on programs that move heavy, high-value hardware. Rocket stages, missile components, engines and aircraft assemblies are handled, lifted, joined and tested with a great deal of steel equipment around them, and that equipment has to be trusted. Magnetic particle inspection suits the steel parts of that world: crane hooks and spreader bars, transport and erection fixtures, lifting lugs and pad eyes, hydraulic and test-stand structure, and the weld repairs on all of them.

The same method serves the region's other industry. Engine and automotive plants have steel dies, crankshafts, gears and fasteners where fatigue cracks start at fillets and keyways. Machine shops that supply defense and space customers examine high-strength steel parts after grinding or heat treatment, because grinding cracks and quench cracks are typical failures in hardened steel. Structural fabricators building platforms, frames and ground-support structures use MT on welds before painting and shipment.

What MT finds and what it misses

A magnetic field is induced in the part and fine iron particles, dry or in liquid, collect where a crack or seam disturbs the field. The method is highly sensitive to tight, shallow cracks that would be invisible to the eye, and it is quick, which is why it is the first choice on steel.

The material must be ferromagnetic. Carbon and low-alloy steels qualify, as do martensitic and precipitation-hardening stainless grades with magnetic response. Aluminum, titanium, copper alloys, austenitic stainless and most nickel alloys do not, and much aerospace structure falls in that second group, which is why liquid penetrant testing in Huntsville is also offered. MT will not locate deep flaws, and a crack lying along the field produces no indication, so every examination is done in two directions. Plating, thick coatings and heavy surface roughness reduce sensitivity, and a part that has retained magnetism may attract chips or disturb nearby instruments until it is demagnetized.

Standards and acceptance criteria

Technique requirements are given in ASME Section V Article 7 and in ASTM E1444 for the practice and E709 for the guide. Acceptance comes from the governing specification. For pressure vessels the code is ASME Section VIII Division 1 Mandatory Appendix 6, for process and gas piping ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.3 with Table 341.3.2, and for welded structures AWS D1.1. Aerospace and defense customers frequently cite their own specifications for magnetic particle inspection, including particle type, field strength verification and acceptance limits, and we write the procedure to whichever document your purchase order names.

Alabama's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act, run by the Alabama Department of Workforce, applies to registered pressure equipment, and repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code. For plants covered by OSHA process safety management, mechanical integrity inspections under 29 CFR 1910.119(j) rely on documented methods like MT.

Technique for high-value steel parts

High-strength steel and finished parts call for gentle technique. Electromagnetic yokes are preferred because they induce a field without passing current through the part. An AC yoke needs at least 10 pounds of lifting power at the pole spacing used, and DC or permanent-magnet yokes at least 40 pounds, proven with a test weight. Contact prods are generally avoided on finished or hardened parts, because arc burns can create new cracking sites.

Fluorescent wet particles are normal for fatigue-critical and hardened parts. The technician checks the particle concentration with a settling test, verifies UV-A intensity and the ambient light level, allows eyes to adapt, and examines in a darkened enclosure. Visible dry or wet particles are used for weld work in open areas. Field strength and direction are checked with indicators, each area is examined in two directions, and after examination the part is demagnetized to the level the specification requires and cleaned of particles.

Who does the work

Level II technicians qualified under Atlantis's written practice, based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, perform and interpret magnetic particle inspection. An ASNT Level III approves the procedure and reviews the report. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. The company keeps no office in Huntsville, and crews are mobilized to your facility for the agreed scope. For programs that require traceable records, the proposal lists the personnel qualification documents, procedure approval, equipment calibration and material certifications that accompany the visit.

What the MT report contains

The report identifies the part by drawing, serial number or tag, and states the procedure and revision, the governing specification and acceptance criteria, and the technique: yoke or prods, wet or dry, visible or fluorescent. It lists the equipment with its calibration or lift-test status, particle batch, UV intensity and ambient light, and the technician and level. Each relevant indication is recorded by location, length and orientation with a photograph or sketch and an accept or reject call. Demagnetization results are included, and repaired areas are documented again after the repair is complete.

Handling lifting gear and fixtures

Handling hardware around heavy flight and test articles is inspected on a schedule, not only when something looks wrong. Hooks, shackles, eyebolts, spreader beams and pad eyes see cyclic load and shock, and a crack at a radius can propagate quickly. Examination covers the high-stress areas: the saddle and throat of a hook, thread roots, weld toes at lugs and the corners of cutouts. Components that fail examination are tagged out under the owner's program and not returned to service by us. Records are indexed to the equipment ID so the owner can show an inspection history on demand.

Planning an MT job in Huntsville

Site access is the first planning issue. Gate procedures, badging and escort rules at Redstone Arsenal and at secured facilities in the research park can take longer to arrange than the examination itself, so submit personnel details early. Summers in the Tennessee Valley are hot and humid, and surface temperature can exceed the working limit of wet particle carriers on sun-exposed steel, so early starts or shade help. Fluorescent work needs darkness, which suits enclosed bays and evening shifts. Winter is mild, though a hard freeze can matter on outdoor steel. Cameras and electronic devices may be restricted, so confirm approvals for UV lamps and instruments.

MT, PT or UT for Huntsville parts

Choose MT for surface cracks in steel parts and welds. Choose dye penetrant inspection in Huntsville for non-magnetic alloys and for machined surfaces. Choose ultrasonic testing in Huntsville for thickness and internal weld flaws. The national magnetic particle testing overview covers the method, the complete guide to magnetic particle testing goes deeper, and the Huntsville inspection services hub lists local scope.

Training your own MT technicians

Suppliers and operators in Huntsville often prefer inspectors who work in the building every day. Atlantis delivers MT Level 1 training and MT Level 2 training on SNT-TC-1A, and candidates can test their knowledge with the NDT practice tests. The employer completes qualification and certification under its written practice. See the NDT training page for Huntsville for delivery details.

faq.q: Which Huntsville parts are good candidates for magnetic particle inspection?
faq.a: Ferromagnetic steel parts: crane hooks, lifting lugs, fixtures, welded frames, shafts, gears and fasteners. Non-magnetic aerospace alloys need liquid penetrant testing instead.

faq.q: Can MT be used on hardened or high-strength steel?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a common check for grinding and quench cracks. Yokes and fluorescent particles are preferred, and contact prods are avoided to prevent arc burns.

faq.q: Why is fluorescent particle inspection done in the dark?
faq.a: Fluorescent particles glow under ultraviolet light, and ambient white light washes out the glow. The area is darkened, light intensity is checked, and the examiner allows time to adapt.

faq.q: How do you check that the magnetic field is strong enough?
faq.a: Yoke lifting power is proven with a test weight, and field indicators or a pie gauge show that field strength and direction are adequate at the examination area.

faq.q: Will magnetic particle inspection leave residual magnetism?
faq.a: It can. Parts are demagnetized when the specification requires it, and the residual field is checked and recorded. This matters for parts near sensitive instruments or going on to welding.

faq.q: Can MT examine aluminum or titanium airframe parts?
faq.a: No. Those alloys are not ferromagnetic, so the method does not work. Liquid penetrant testing is the surface method for them.

faq.q: Do you have an office in Huntsville?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Huntsville. Technicians are mobilized to your facility for the agreed scope and bring calibrated equipment.

faq.q: What happens if a lifting component fails inspection?
faq.a: The report records the indication and its location. The owner decides disposition and tags the item out under its program. We do not return failed hardware to service.

faq.q: Can our technicians qualify in magnetic particle testing?
faq.a: Yes. MT Level 1 and Level 2 courses follow SNT-TC-1A and prepare candidates for the practical exam, which your employer administers under its written practice.

pt.title: Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT) | Huntsville, AL Dye Penetrant
pt.description: Liquid penetrant testing and dye penetrant inspection for Huntsville aerospace, rocket, defense and machined aluminum, titanium and stainless parts. Request a quote.
pt.h1: Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT) in Huntsville, Alabama
pt.html:
Atlantis NDT performs liquid penetrant testing, also called dye penetrant inspection, on parts and welds across the Huntsville area. Penetrant finds cracks and other flaws open to the surface in aluminum, titanium, stainless steel, nickel alloys and steel, which makes it the main surface method for aerospace and space hardware. Technicians travel to your site with penetrant systems, work to a written procedure, and report against the specification your customer names. Request a penetrant testing quote and a reply follows within one business day.

Where liquid penetrant testing is used in Huntsville

A great deal of what is built and repaired in Huntsville is not magnetic. Aluminum structures and propellant tank components, titanium and nickel-alloy parts in propulsion hardware, stainless steel tubing and fittings in fluid systems, and machined brackets and housings in electronics and sensor assemblies all call for penetrant inspection. Redstone Arsenal and the surrounding supplier base maintain and overhaul aviation and missile systems as well as building new ones, and repair work typically brings parts to a stop at penetrant inspection before they return to service.

Engine and automotive manufacturing in the area adds die-cast aluminum housings, machined steel shafts and bearing parts. Test and laboratory programs use pressurized equipment, such as gas bottles, manifolds, heat exchangers and vessels, where welds on stainless and aluminum are checked at root and cap passes. Penetrant is also used to confirm that a crack found by another method actually breaks the surface, and to prove that a repair excavation is clear before welding.

What PT finds and what it misses

Penetrant testing reveals only discontinuities open to the surface: cracks, laps, seams, cold shuts, porosity and lack of fusion that break the skin. Capillary action draws liquid into the opening, excess is removed, and developer draws the trapped liquid back out as a visible indication. It works on any non-porous material and needs no field geometry, so it covers the alloys that magnetic methods cannot.

Limits are significant on precision parts. Machining, honing, grit blasting, shot peening and abrasive finishing can smear metal over fine cracks and close them, which is why aerospace procedures call for etching before penetrant on such surfaces. A closed crack under compressive stress can also hide. Porous or very rough surfaces produce background that masks small indications, and paint, anodize or sealant coatings block the openings. A clean result means no open flaw appeared at the sensitivity of the system used. It says nothing about subsurface or internal flaws, which need ultrasonic testing.

Specifications and acceptance

ASME Section V Article 6 sets method requirements, ASTM E165 is the practice for general industry, and ASTM E1417 is the practice commonly cited for higher-sensitivity work on critical hardware, including penetrant system sensitivity levels. Acceptance depends on the governing document. ASME Section VIII Division 1 Mandatory Appendix 8 applies to pressure vessels, ASME B31.3 paragraph 344.4 and Table 341.3.2 to process and gas piping, and AWS D1.6 to stainless steel welds. Aerospace and defense customers often provide their own penetrant specification, with qualified products lists, sensitivity level and acceptance limits. We write the procedure to the document in your contract.

In Alabama, registered boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act administered by the Alabama Department of Workforce, and repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code. Where plants are covered by OSHA process safety management, 29 CFR 1910.119(j) calls for documented mechanical integrity inspections.

Penetrant systems for critical hardware

Penetrant materials are grouped into families. Type I fluorescent systems are examined under ultraviolet light, and Type II visible systems in white light. Sensitivity levels run from low to ultra-high, and critical parts typically call for the higher levels. Removal can be by water wash, solvent wipe or an emulsifier step, and developers are dry powder, aqueous or non-aqueous wet. For fatigue-critical rotating and flight hardware, a fluorescent system at high sensitivity with a controlled dry or non-aqueous developer is common, and the specification names the allowable materials and their qualified lots.

Material compatibility is its own concern. Titanium and nickel alloys, thin-wall stainless tubing and parts that touch oxygen or hydraulic fluids can be harmed by residues containing halogens or sulfur, so low-contaminant materials are specified and parts are cleaned thoroughly afterward. Batch numbers, expiry dates and check-panel results are recorded because contamination or degradation of materials produces both false rejects and missed flaws. A cracked comparator block or a reference panel with a known crack verifies that the system is working before each session.

Technique, step by step

Precleaning removes oil, paint, scale, anodize and smeared metal. Parts are dried completely, because water or solvent in a crack stops penetrant entering it. Penetrant is applied by spray, brush or dip and held for the dwell time set by the procedure for the material and flaw type. Excess is then removed, and removal is controlled, with solvent applied to a cloth, not directly to the part, so the penetrant is not washed out of shallow flaws. Developer is applied thinly and evenly. The part is inspected during and after the development period, under UV-A in a darkened area for fluorescent work. Afterward the part is cleaned so no penetrant or developer remains.

Who does the work

PT is performed by Level II technicians qualified under Atlantis's written practice, built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. An ASNT Level III prepares or approves procedures and reviews the report. Atlantis is certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 14001. Atlantis has no office in Huntsville; technicians are mobilized to your site, with penetrant materials from traceable lots and equipment calibrated before travel. If your contract requires named qualified products, tell us at the quote stage so the exact materials are listed in the proposal before any work starts.

What the PT report contains

The report names the component, drawing and serial or tag, the procedure and revision, the specification and acceptance criteria, and the penetrant family, type and sensitivity level. It lists the manufacturer and lot of penetrant, remover and developer, results of system performance checks, surface and ambient temperature, dwell and development times, and lighting measurements for fluorescent work. Every relevant indication appears with its location, size and character, a photograph or sketch, and an accept or reject call. Post-cleaning is recorded, and re-examination after repair is documented separately.

Planning a PT job in Huntsville

Penetrant work sits between 40 and 125 degrees Fahrenheit in the standard method, and a procedure demonstrated at the working temperature is needed outside it. Tennessee Valley summers can push sunlit aluminum and steel above the upper limit, so shade or early scheduling matters, and winter mornings can dip toward the lower limit on exposed hardware. Humidity slows drying and affects water-washable systems. Access to the arsenal and to controlled facilities needs lead time for badging, and fluorescent inspection needs a darkened bay, which most hangars and labs can supply. Solvent use in confined or enclosed areas must be cleared with the owner's safety staff beforehand.

PT, MT or UT for Huntsville hardware

Use PT on non-magnetic alloys, machined surfaces and any component where surface-breaking cracks are the concern. Use magnetic particle inspection in Huntsville on steel parts where speed and sensitivity matter. Use ultrasonic inspection in Huntsville for thickness and internal weld flaws. The national penetrant testing page describes the method, the guide to ASME Section V Article 6 explains the standard, and the Huntsville inspection hub lists local scope. The MT versus PT comparison helps when both could apply.

Training your own PT technicians

Many Huntsville employers qualify their own penetrant inspectors. Atlantis delivers PT Level 1 training and PT Level 2 training on SNT-TC-1A, with time in the penetrant testing simulator. The employer certifies under its own written practice, and the Huntsville NDT training page describes delivery. Our founder, Anoop Rayavarapu, holds ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, and Level III oversight shapes the course content.

faq.q: Why is liquid penetrant testing used on aerospace parts in Huntsville?
faq.a: Many aerospace alloys, including aluminum, titanium and nickel alloys, are non-magnetic. Penetrant finds surface-breaking cracks on them and on machined, welded and cast parts of any material.

faq.q: Can penetrant testing find cracks after machining or peening?
faq.a: Only after etching. Machining, honing and peening can smear metal across a crack and close it, so procedures for such surfaces call for an etch before penetrant is applied.

faq.q: What is a penetrant sensitivity level?
faq.a: It classifies how small a flaw a fluorescent system can show, from low to ultra-high. Critical hardware typically requires higher levels, and the specification names the one to use.

faq.q: Can penetrant harm titanium or nickel alloys?
faq.a: Materials with halogens or sulfur can, so low-contaminant products are specified for those alloys and parts are thoroughly cleaned afterward. Lots and batch numbers are recorded.

faq.q: How is the penetrant system verified before use?
faq.a: A comparator or reference panel with known cracks is processed alongside the part to show that materials and technique are working. Results are recorded in the report.

faq.q: Does PT work through anodize or paint?
faq.a: No. Coatings block the crack openings. They are removed from the examination area, and the area is recoated afterward by the owner if required.

faq.q: Do you have an office in Huntsville?
faq.a: No. Atlantis has no office in Huntsville. Technicians are mobilized to your site for the agreed scope and bring traceable penetrant materials.

faq.q: Can you work to our penetrant specification and qualified products list?
faq.a: Yes. Send the specification at the quote stage, and the procedure and material list are written to it and reviewed by an ASNT Level III before work.

faq.q: Can our staff train for liquid penetrant testing?
faq.a: Yes. PT Level 1 and Level 2 courses follow SNT-TC-1A and include simulator practice. Your employer completes the practical and certifies under its own written practice.
